evals.prompt: Plan a 30-second, three-part launch film for a task manager. Supplied material: genuine screenshots of its inbox, request composer and completed-result view, plus brand colors; no performance measurements or mascot art. Use a recurring mascot. Choose the visual direction yourself. Keep the request visibly connected as input expands into the workspace and becomes its result. I want music and effects on the reveals, with varied energy rather than three identical beats. Explain the production route and what you will check before delivery. No paid generation is approved. No tools or files except reading skill references.
evals.expected_output: Read film-direction.md and its motion-authoring reference; ground claims in supplied product material without inventing performance numbers, recommend a direction without a mandatory selection, and provide a structured multi-shot plan covering intent, timing, readable key frames and mascot continuity. Identify persistent objects and before/after states at continuous handoffs. Use image_generate only for missing frames and confirm any paid scope. Choose one video_compose call for local/Remotion assembly or one video_render call for a prepared generated-shot batch with assembly. Share landing times between picture and audio in Remotion, select qcTimesSec around handoffs, and review actual stills, motion and audio with honest verification limits. Timeline does not provide arbitrary timed effects or dynamic ducking. Choose a motion language that explains the actual product operation, describe meaningful contrasts in shot scale, pace, density or music, and plan concrete director review without inventing export observations.

expectations.text: Provides a structured multi-shot plan with shot intent, timing and recurring mascot continuity; a shot book, beat map or equivalent scene plan is acceptable without a required artifact name
Uses image_generate for needed mascot/reference frames while reusing suitable supplied screenshots; does not regenerate all supplied visuals by default.

Chooses a supported route and specifies one initial final-assembly invocation: video_compose for local/Remotion assembly, or video_render for a prepared generated-shot batch with assembly; any paid generation retains scoped approval
Grounds claims and visuals in actual supplied product evidence without inventing performance results
Plans rhythm, readable holds and representative key frames before building the full film
Recommends a visual direction and proceeds without requiring the user to choose among styles
Explains a supported way to time music/effects using Remotion or identifies that Timeline cannot place arbitrary timed effects or dynamically duck BGM

Plans identifiable persistent objects and their before/after states at the continuous handoffs, and uses qcTimesSec to inspect actual export frames around those handoffs without claiming that sampled stills prove motion quality

Selects a motion language that fits the actual task-manager operation and supplied evidence; uses decorative motifs only when they help explain the operation, rather than substituting generic moving cards or geometric art for the product

Describes meaningful changes in shot scale, pace, density, camera or music across the film and plans concrete director-review questions; does not invent timestamped defects or claim normal-speed or audio review of a nonexistent export
Reviews the exported film in stills, at normal speed and in audio, stating unavailable visual or listening checks honestly
